skill.name: excalidraw-diagram-generator
skill.description: Generate Excalidraw-format diagrams from natural language descriptions, including flowcharts, mind maps, relationship diagrams, architecture diagrams, DFDs, swimlanes, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, and ER diagrams.
skill.summary: Creates editable Excalidraw diagrams from natural language prompts.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, diagram labels, template URLs, or documentation examples. The confirmed risk is limited to helper scripts that write user-selected diagram or library files. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, hidden network behavior, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts write to paths supplied on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain writes to expected .excalidraw and library directories, validate extensions, and warn before overwriting or renaming files.

remediation.issue: The library splitter expands user-provided .excalidrawlib files into many generated files.
remediation.suggestion: Add size and item-count limits before writing icons, and document that untrusted libraries should be reviewed first.

content.value_statement: Clear diagrams take time to build by hand. This skill turns structured prompts into editable Excalidraw files for processes, systems, data, and ideas.
actual_capabilities: Creates .excalidraw JSON files from natural language diagram requests.
Supports flowcharts, relationship diagrams, mind maps, architecture diagrams, DFDs, swimlanes, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, and ER diagrams.
Uses bundled templates for common diagram types.
Documents required Excalidraw element properties, styling, and font settings.
Includes Python helpers for splitting Excalidraw libraries and adding icons or arrows to diagrams.
Provides guidance for optional icon libraries from Excalidraw.
limitations: It does not embed images during automatic diagram generation.
Large diagrams should be split because the skill recommends fewer than 20 elements.
Icon workflows require users to provide valid Excalidraw library files.
The helper scripts can modify local diagram and library files.

use_cases.title: Visualize Product Workflows
use_cases.description: Convert a user journey, approval flow, or onboarding process into an editable Excalidraw flowchart.

use_cases.title: Map System Architecture
use_cases.description: Create component diagrams, data flow diagrams, or cloud architecture drafts from a written system description.

use_cases.title: Organize Learning Concepts
use_cases.description: Turn topics, branches, and supporting details into a mind map for planning or teaching.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Flowchart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw flowchart for this process: [steps]. Keep it under 10 steps and include clear labels.

prompt_templates.title: Map Entity Relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw relationship diagram for these entities: [entities]. Show each relationship and label every connection.

prompt_templates.title: Design a System Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw architecture diagram for this system: [description]. Group components by layer and show data flow direction.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Icon Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excalidraw cloud diagram using available icon libraries. First verify the library reference, then add icons and arrows for [components].

output_examples.input: Create a flowchart for user registration with email verification and password setup.
output_examples.output: A saved user-registration-flow.excalidraw file with start, email entry, verification, password setup, and completion steps.

output_examples.input: Diagram User, Post, and Comment relationships for a content platform.
output_examples.output: An editable relationship diagram showing User creates Post, User writes Comment, and Post contains Comment.

output_examples.input: Make a mind map of machine learning concepts for a study session.
output_examples.output: A central Machine Learning node with branches for supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and deep learning topics.

best_practices: Keep diagrams focused on the main elements before adding details.
Provide entities, relationships, and direction of flow in the prompt.
Use optional icon libraries only after confirming the library reference exists.
anti_patterns: Do not request very large diagrams with many small labels in one file.
Do not use icon workflows without a valid Excalidraw library file.
Do not overwrite existing diagrams without using the edit-suffix workflow or a backup.

faq.question: What file format does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates .excalidraw files that can be opened in Excalidraw or compatible editors.

faq.question: Can it make flowcharts?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports flowcharts, decision paths, and sequential workflow diagrams.

faq.question: Can it use AWS or cloud icons?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user provides a valid Excalidraw library and runs the included splitter workflow.

faq.question: Does it automatically choose a layout?
faq.answer: It provides layout guidance and templates, but it does not run automatic collision detection.

faq.question: Can diagrams be edited after generation?
faq.answer: Yes. The output is an editable Excalidraw file.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Basic diagram generation does not require internet access. Optional library downloads happen outside the skill workflow.
